title: Petro working edits mutate the shared canonical-run cache
current_behavior: from_run assigns the cached LasFile depth, curves dictionary, units and descriptions directly to WellData. run returns the same mutable object to subsequent callers.
impact: Readers can obtain different scientific values from the same canonical curve depending on whether they request a run or an individual curve. A working edit can become visible before database publication; reload order then affects the answer.
reproduction: Import GR=[1,2,3]. Build WellData.from_run(curve_store.run(...)). Set working GR[0]=99. Another run reader returns 99, while curve_store.read returns the committed value 1. No database save occurs in the probe.
minimal_fix: Give the editable Petro workspace its own dictionaries and arrays, and define cached runs as immutable snapshots or return defensive copies. Preserve explicit canonical publication and revision notification.
regression_test: Edit a Petro working curve with two readers open; assert all committed readers remain unchanged until save, all agree after save, and discard/reload restores the database values.

title: Deleting an imported curve leaves old values in cached runs and a ghost in rebuilt runs
current_behavior: The run stamp uses the axis timestamp and MAX(curve.modified_at). Deleting a non-latest curve need not change either. Fresh reconstruction retains the original header width/names even when a curve row is gone.
impact: A deleted log can remain scientifically usable with its former samples in a warm cache. After cache eviction it changes to an all-NaN ghost instead of disappearing. Canonical list/resolve and run consumers disagree.
reproduction: Prime a run containing GR and RT, delete GR through delete_curve, then resolve GR and read the run. resolve returns none; the cached run still contains [1,2,3]. Direct database reconstruction still lists GR, now all NaN.
minimal_fix: Advance a run revision on every membership/edit operation, invalidate affected run snapshots, and rebuild the run header/column list from surviving canonical rows rather than the original inventory.
regression_test: Prime and unprime readers; delete first/middle/latest/all curves; verify identical surviving names, metadata and values before and after close/reopen. Include LAS export and Petro consumers.

title: Curve depth cache omits the well-unit dependency
current_behavior: arrays returns depth converted to the current well depth unit but caches it using only project path, curve ID and curve timestamp. Updating the well unit does not change that cache key.
impact: Scientific consumers can receive feet-valued depths while the well is now in metres. This changes zone alignment, interpolation and depth-based integration until a cache clear, even when the underlying curve is unchanged.
reproduction: Read a feet-axis curve at [100,101,102], change elevation_units to m, read again: [100,101,102]. Clear the curve cache and read: [30.48,30.7848,31.0896]. The same committed database state yields two different axes.
minimal_fix: Include axis revision and target well unit in cache identity, or explicitly invalidate on those changes. Fetch current record metadata when a previously held CurveRecord is used.
regression_test: Exercise feet↔metres with warm/cold caches and separate database connections; compare every consumer to explicit conversion without requiring a manual forget call.

title: Volumetrics validation differs by mode and admits impossible or non-finite results
current_behavior: Only Manual calls _check_fraction. Polygon/Grid accept porosity=35 v/v. Uniform calculations accept negative net pay, and the FVF test fvf<=0 does not reject NaN.
impact: A common percent-entry mistake produces a plausible-looking but 175-times inflated oil volume in mapped modes. Negative thickness produces negative reserves; NaN Bo produces a NaN report instead of refusing the calculation.
reproduction: With A=150 acres,h=65 ft,Sw=.25,Bo=1.2: Polygon porosity=35 v/v returns 1,654,635,937.5 STB instead of rejecting it. Manual correctly rejects that fraction, but h=-65 returns -9,455,062.5 STB and Bo=NaN returns NaN.
minimal_fix: Use shared finite/range validation at the active-input boundary for all modes: fractions 0–1, physical thickness policy explicit, positive finite active FVF. Flag invalid grid cells with counts or reject the calculation under an explicit policy; do not guess percent conversion.
regression_test: Run the same invalid cases through all three modes and UI/scenario loading: NaN/Inf, negative thickness, phi/Sw/NTG outside 0–1, zero/negative FVF, explicit % controls, and valid boundary values.

title: Directional survey imports discard explicit depth units
current_behavior: The survey reader skips a units row as nonnumeric and Survey carries no source-unit field. Imported station numbers are stored in the well depth system without conversion or a mismatch check.
impact: A metric survey can silently be interpreted in feet, changing MD/TVD, BHL offsets and subsequent geological positioning. The angles and minimum-curvature algorithm can be correct while the physical trajectory is wrong.
reproduction: Import MD,Inc,Azi with an explicit (m),(deg),(deg) row and stations 0 and 100 into a feet well. The stored final MD/TVD are 100 ft; the file specifies 100 m, equivalent to 328.0839895 ft.
minimal_fix: Carry explicit source length units through parsing and convert all length columns to the well unit before storage; where the file is ambiguous require an explicit import choice or reject rather than infer magnitude.
regression_test: Single-well and bulk imports for metre/feet/US-survey-foot sources, both angular and positional station formats, including mismatched and absent units and transaction rollback on rejection.

title: Seismic synthetic input units are still inferred from magnitude
current_behavior: Unknown-unit sonic values are divided by feet-per-metre when their median exceeds 250. Density is divided by 1000 when its median exceeds 100, even if the provided unit explicitly says g/cc.
impact: This is a live scientific unit transformation based on data magnitude. Bad or ambiguously labelled values become seemingly valid impedance inputs; output timing and amplitudes can change silently. It is distinct from percent scaling and from display-only range selection.
reproduction: density_gcc([2500], "g/cc") returns [2.5]. slowness_us_per_ft([328.084], "") guesses metres and returns about 100 us/ft. The existing sonic test explicitly encodes the latter guess.
minimal_fix: Honor recognized explicit units and reject invalid values in those units. For absent/unknown units, request a source-unit choice with provenance; remove the magnitude fallback and revise the legacy expectation test.
regression_test: Explicit g/cc must never trigger kg/m³ conversion; test absent/unknown units, explicit kg/m³ and us/m conversions, bad ranges, and the UI path into a synthetic.
classification: Confirmed code behavior — violates explicit-unit requirement

title: Calculated curve IDs change on every Petro-state save and immediately break provenance
current_behavior: Saving calculated curves deletes every calc row for the well, then inserts replacements with new AUTOINCREMENT IDs. The shared CurveRecord contract describes IDs as stable; derived provenance stores parent IDs.
impact: Deriving B from calculated A can invalidate the parent identity during the very save that creates B. Held record IDs and provenance become stale even though A was not deleted by the user.
reproduction: Create calculated A (ID 3), derive B. A now has ID 4, get(3) returns none, and B.parents still contains [3].
minimal_fix: Update existing calculated rows in place keyed by their stable identity; insert only new curves and delete only intentionally removed curves. Preserve IDs across metadata-only workspace saves.
regression_test: Derive from a calculated parent, save/reopen, rename/edit a sibling, and assert parent IDs still resolve and all provenance links remain valid.

title: Canonical curve updates accept arrays that do not match the depth axis
current_behavior: Imported curve updates store arbitrary-length values without checking their axis length. arrays later detects the mismatch and returns none.
impact: A successful update can make a previously usable scientific curve disappear from canonical readers. The invalid payload is durable; the old values are overwritten rather than rejected.
reproduction: Import a three-sample RT curve; update it with [8,9]. Two samples are committed against a three-sample axis and curve_store.read returns none.
minimal_fix: Validate dimensionality and axis length before entering the write transaction; reject mismatched replacements while retaining old data. Keep sample/range metadata consistent.
regression_test: Reject short, long, scalar and multidimensional replacements with byte-identical old data; permit a valid aligned update and verify across reopen and all reader paths.

title: Unsafe named-repository paths escape through the placeholder fallback
current_behavior: The resolver correctly returns Unsafe repository path with path=None for an absolute relative component. placeholder then appends the raw component to a Path; an absolute component discards the placeholder prefix.
impact: A rejected repository reference can still resolve to a real file outside its repository through the suite-wide database adapter. This defeats asset containment. The probe establishes read access; arbitrary execution or destructive deletion is not established.
reproduction: Create a harmless temporary outside.txt and resolve @repository/TEST//tmp/.../outside.txt. Repository status is Unsafe, but db.resolve_path returns that absolute fixture and it is readable, even without a configured root.
minimal_fix: Do not turn an unsafe resolution into a filesystem path. Return a typed missing/unsafe result or raise at the adapter; if compatibility requires a placeholder, construct it only from sanitized display text and never concatenate untrusted path components.
regression_test: Exercise the database adapter and actual grid/raster/seismic loaders, not only repositories.resolve, with POSIX absolutes, Windows drives/UNC paths, traversal and symlink escapes. None may open an outside sentinel.

title: Gridded volumetrics integrates invalid crossed polygon boundaries
current_behavior: The constants-only polygon route checks polygon_stats validity. The gridded route sends the same boundary coordinates directly to point-in-polygon testing without validating the ring.
impact: A self-crossing outline has no unambiguous reservoir interior, yet one mode reports volumes while the other refuses it. An edited saved boundary can silently alter included cells.
reproduction: Use a 3×3 constant net-pay grid with the bow-tie boundary [(0,0),(200,200),(0,200),(200,0)]. Grid mode accepts it, includes two cells and reports 28,941.1157 STB.
minimal_fix: Validate boundary and compartment drawings using the shared geometry rules before integration, including closed-state checks at scenario resolution; refuse ambiguous geometry with its reason.
regression_test: Crossed, open, degenerate and non-finite outlines in both constant and gridded Polygon/Grid modes, including editing a previously valid stored drawing.

title: PDF raster publication overwrites the image before sidecar success
current_behavior: write saves directly to the final TIFF path, then writes the provenance sidecar. There is no staged publication or rollback across those operations.
impact: If the sidecar write fails, the import raises after replacing an existing image. A preexisting sidecar can describe old content and the UI does not complete registration. Interruption during TIFF encoding also risks a partial destination.
reproduction: Place previous bytes at an existing .tif target. Inject an OSError only at sidecar write_text. write raises, but previous bytes are gone and a new TIFF exists without its sidecar.
minimal_fix: Stage the TIFF and JSON separately, validate them, and use the existing safeio publication/rollback service before registration. Preserve both previous outputs on failure.
regression_test: Failure injection at encoding, sidecar writing, promotion and registration boundaries, verifying old asset/provenance bytes and DB references remain coherent.
classification: Confirmed failure-handling defect — reproduced with injected I/O failure

title: Short seismic synthetics have mismatched time and trace lengths
current_behavior: np.convolve(rc,w,mode="same") returns max(len(rc),len(w)), not necessarily the number of time samples. The time axis remains n samples.
impact: Short valid log intervals can fail interpolation or plotting, making a synthetic unavailable for that interval. This is a shape defect rather than a demonstrated wrong geological formula.
reproduction: Ten time samples with default 128 ms wavelet and 1 ms sampling produce len(time)=10 and len(trace)=129. correlate uses those as xp/fp of np.interp.
minimal_fix: Center the full convolution onto exactly the intended time-axis length, preserving alignment and polarity. Keep time/impedance/RC/trace shapes equal.
regression_test: Intervals shorter than, equal to and longer than the wavelet, odd/even lengths, an impulse with a hand-known peak location, and synthetic-window plotting/correlation.

title: Affine georeferencing accepts a singular map transform with near-zero RMS
current_behavior: Affine fitting rejects collinear image control points but does not reject a singular fitted 2×2 map transform. inverse detects a zero determinant only later.
impact: Collinear map control points can appear to fit perfectly while collapsing the raster onto a line; the reported RMS is misleading as a usability check.
reproduction: Image controls (0,0),(1,0),(0,1) mapped to (0,0),(1,0),(2,0) produce determinant 0 and RMS approximately 5.8e-16.
minimal_fix: Validate finite coefficients, nondegenerate map controls and a scale-aware determinant/condition threshold before returning an accepted Fit. Report why the transform cannot be used.
regression_test: Collinear map points, identical map points, near-singular controls, valid reflected/rotated/sheared affine transforms, and disabled-point behavior.

title: Tk font cache survives root destruction and reuses a dead interpreter
current_behavior: The process-wide cache key uses str(root), often simply ".". A new Tk interpreter with that same name receives the old Font object, which retains its old Tcl interpreter.
impact: Repeated root creation in tests/embedding can return an unusable font and retain dead roots. Normal Toplevel windows sharing one live root do not establish the same failure.
reproduction: Create root A, cache a font, destroy A, create root B and request the same style. The same object is returned and actual() raises application has been destroyed.
minimal_fix: Scope fonts by interpreter/root identity with lifecycle cleanup (prefer a per-root cache); avoid strong global retention of destroyed roots.
regression_test: Destroy/recreate two roots with the same Tk pathname and prove the returned font belongs to the new interpreter and old cached roots can be released.

title: Raster overlay still infers a percent-like display range from magnitude
current_behavior: Neutron/density-porosity overlay limits are multiplied by 100 when the maximum exceeds 1.5, as well as for explicit percent/pu units.
impact: This can choose a misleading visual range for outliers or unusual curves. It changes limits, not scientific samples, and is not equivalent to a scientific percent-conversion defect.
reproduction: Supply a decimal-family choice with maximum above 1.5 and no percent unit; default limits switch to the percent-style range.
minimal_fix: Use explicit units and saved/user-selected scale for display defaults; preserve stored samples and user track settings.
regression_test: Decimal curves with large outliers and low-magnitude percent curves choose limits from metadata/controls, while value arrays remain byte-identical.
